utterances.text: Crater analysis by itself, not as a course. But in an army, I have undergone, I think, eight, nine, ten courses. So even in the very basic course, they do give us a know-how of the crater analysis. But certainly, it is meant for the specialist for a particular arm. And from infantries, we don't have to do crater analysis. But I had an idea, and it was in the basic training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So would you say that are you familiar with the fundamentals of crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes, you can say the basics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were posted in Hrasnica. I'm going to -- well, firstly, why don't you start by telling the Court what were your duties with the UNMO team, Sierra India 1.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Can I have water, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: You asked me regarding my tasks in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Hrasnica, number one, was that we had to patrol the area. Number two was there was one OP. It was basically manned by the French soldiers, and we also used to go there just for about two, three, hours in the evening, daily. Number three was reporting of the incidents in case there was an explosion or firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "OP," do you mean observation point?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah, observation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thanks. And from that observation point, what were you able to observe, generally, first?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: From observation point, it was located, if I may recall, on the start of the track, which used to be at that time known as Gunway Road. It is on the Igman hill. And from where it started, just about, I think, after about 100 or 200 metres, it was a little higher than the normal place. So from that place, I think, we could see very clearly a place known as Ilidza; then a general area of Butmir Sokolovic; and to some extent - I would not say very clearly - but to some extent, I would say probably to the right, I'm forgetting the name, that was given a number also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine. Let me just ask you, if I was show you a map, would you be able to, approximately, mark the location of this observation point?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Approximately, yes. It may not be 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could have 65 ter 2738 brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Colonel, in a moment, a map will appear on the screen in front of you, and I will ask you a few questions. While that is loading, maybe I can ask you a question. You mentioned that you can see clearly a place known as Ilidza. Do you know whether the army of Republika Srpska or the ABiH controlled that area?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Sorry, say again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The place of Ilidza, this is a place that you said you could see from the observation point. Can you tell the Court which party the conflict controlled that area?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I think it was Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. We have the map now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If the bottom left-hand section could be enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Colonel, can you see that map?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you see Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I can't see Hrasnica written anywhere. Just point it out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can scroll down to the bottom left, so we can get that whole section. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that clearer, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can it be enlarged further, is that possible? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How about that?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I can see it clearer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay, fabulous. Can I just take the pen which the court usher will give you and mark the place Hrasnica, please.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Just the Hrasnica, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. For the moment, Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if could you now, with a cross, just mark the location of the observation point that you have earlier spoken about?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Okay. It may not be 100 per cent correct. What I recollect is that at the end of Hrasnica, on the left, it used to go up. If this is Igman, so probably it was somewhere here. It was close to the convoy road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And the convoy road, can you --

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I don't know if marking is correct or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's okay. Can you mark with the letter R the location of the convoy road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, that probably this could be in this, like this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was further right, even including this, what do you call it, Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just with respect to this convoy road, who -- in your time there, who used that road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was used, I think, by everybody, by the civilian workers, by the UN vehicles. I think there was certainly NGOs who also used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how significant or how important was this road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I think it was probably the most important. As I know it, this was the only road available for communicating with the Sarajevo from this side. That was the only place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that you would go to the observation point?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think you said a few hours every day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what was it specifically that you observed when you were there?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Basically, I observed, for one, it was very close to the convoy road, so we could see the movement on that road. Number two, any firing incident, because the firing incident in those days were mostly in this area. Any movement on this was fired upon from a position in the [indiscernible]. So that was one reporting of the incidents, the number of vehicles moving, and at a time -- they is were timed. It wasn't -- everybody can't go there. So the time was given that from this place to this time to this time, a particular convoy is going do be move. It could be civilian convoy. It could be any other convoy. So we used to observe that. And number two [sic], in front, it was a higher place. So in front in case, there was any firing incident or maybe some movement if that is visible at that time, that was also reported upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Firstly, let me ask you, how -- the view or -- yes the view from the observation point how good was it?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Up to Ilidza, it was okay. We could even find the -- lots of people were moving. But certainly the skeletons and the general movement, we could feel it. You could see with naked eye. We had the binoculars also. But even with naked eye, up to Ilidza, yes. Not towards right side, towards left side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that -- you said in those days there was firing from positions, I think you said in Ilidza; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That you saw -- that you observed firing from positions in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Firstly, do you recall what -- briefly tell the Court, what did you see being fired from Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: The only thing I'm very sure that there was either the 12.7 or the 14.5 rifle firing in the direction of the convoy road. I mean that was very normal. If there were any vehicle moving on this, rest assured that it will be fired upon. So that was one. And other than this, there were certain mortar rockets fired from this area to the general direction of the track which was going to the Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you firstly mark -- you have already marked the Igman road. Can you mark that track "going to the Sarajevo," as you have stated?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I was there for only, I think, three, four months, and it is over now 12 years. I may not be 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Generally, I know that if this is the airport, it used to cross on this side, going like this one; and then maybe somewhere here, we think this is convoy road or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Age so you said that mortars from Ilidza would fire on that track; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me ask you how did you know it was a mortar being fired from Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Number one, as I said, even with the naked eye, you can find the positions. Mortar is a weapon that has its different select. You can even find it out on ground, if it is being fired upon from a particular place and when you are located at such a position. So that is one. Number two is it has a different type of trajectory, the weapon itself. It is not a direct firing weapon. So on that clue by itself indicates the type of weapon, the loop of the trajectory that makes the rocket makes. And then even the distances where it falls, that also indicates that it can't be a very long range weapon, or something. So mortars were certainly a small range weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that you used to go to the observation point at I think you said in the evening.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah, at night. Evening, at night, I mean, say, 7.00, 8.00, that was the time. The exact times were not there. Maybe one hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I take it then that while you were there, it was -- well, was it dark?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes. It was dark, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is there anything about -- well, did the darkness or the lack of light assist you in any way in determining that mortars were being fired from Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Maybe you can say -- for sure the 12.7 and 14.5, they have the tracers. So you can clearly find from this place that it is being fired and where it is retained So that is for sure. In case of mortar, you can't say. They don't have the tracer, where generally the point of impact or when it is fired, maybe a small little flash. So that is one thing. But for sure, 12.7, yes, tracers were being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on this road that you marked, this track going to the airport, in your time in Hrasnica, who used that road? What kind of vehicles travelled on that road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I'll say almost all kinds of vehicle. I can't specify, but these were being checked by the UN, closer to airport and closer to Sarajevo. Only the designated and the [indiscernible] were allowed to go to Sarajevo. They were the only ones who were permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps my question wasn't precise enough. Were there -- was this road exclusively used by military, or were there also civilian vehicles using that road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I would say for all, for all. For everybody, not exclusively. But at that time, I mean, the civilian traffic was comparatively lesser.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said "not exclusively," so are you saying civilians did use that road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly, when I say it was NGOs and people who were being fired on that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you saw from Ilidza that road being hit, being targeted. Was it -- from your observation, is it your view that civilians were also being targeted on that road?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I would not say specifically that it was meant for the civilians. Any vehicle driving on that road was being fired on, whether it was civilian, whether UN, or whether it was somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask you to, if you can see it on there, can you just mark with an I the location of Ilidza, please.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was somewhere here. I can't see it. Generally, I think this would be the area. This one maybe, if it is the one ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this still be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P634, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Colonel, I now want to concentrate on the area of Hrasnica. That is where you were posted. Firstly, to your knowledge, and while you were there, were there any military barracks or installations in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Frankly, I, in person, have never visited any of the barracks. But one of the captains, he was -- I think the name was Captain Mustafa. He used to come to our team, just for the -- asking for any administration or some help. So that indicated that maybe -- and he used to introduce himself among the staff officers. Whether that is correct or not, I cannot say because I have not visited any of the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, do you know if there were barracks in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you, while you were there, ever see Bosnian government or Bosnian army mortars being fired from -- from the residential area of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you ever see Bosnian army tanks in that area in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: No. Yes, I only say, one day we heard there were some tanks. We went, not me but my teammates, went outside to see there were no tanks. I haven't seen a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know who you heard that from?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I remember it was the interpreter or somebody from -- or the landlord at the house that we were living in. They said, We had seen some tanks, and immediately the team members went outside, but there was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So upon that information, members of your team went outside to confirm?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And they did not see --

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: No, they did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you in a bit more detail in a moment, but did something happen to you on the 1st of July, 1995 in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes. 1st of July, there was explosion outside our accommodation, and I was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. And I said I will just get to that topic in a moment. But I want to ask you where you were; in other words, where your team was in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: We were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just one second, sorry. The place where you were, were there -- in that vicinity, were there any military facilities, military vehicles in the vicinity of that place?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Does that include the UN also?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, no. I mean really from the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Not in the close vicinity. I can't say. I'm very sure not on, say, five to seven houses on both sides. It was a civilian area, and our house was somewhere in the centre. Not there, not in that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, when you conducted -- well, let me ask you, did you conduct investigations into shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And these incidents that you conducted investigations on, were they incidents that involved civilians -- were they incidents that involved civilians or military personnel?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was only civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you conduct the your investigation, what -- what did you or your team members what did you do?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I couldn't get your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What exactly was your role when it came to these investigations?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Oh, okay. When the moment, we used to hear all the time reported by somebody, so we used to rush to that area, the area of impact. And there was a form. We had to fill it, and you had to include the area of impact, the time of incident, and the damages, the injuries, casualties. Casualties, I mean, at times were there when we used to reach; and at other times, they were removed from that place and we might have to go to the hospital or the morgue. So all these things were to be reported there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you talk about casualties, if, as you say, they weren't at the scene, was it routine for the -- for you and your team members to visit the hospitals to confirm the casualties?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: In a way, yes. No where was it written that we must go to hospital and to the morgue, but we had to report the casualties so we used to go to those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it you personally did that on occasion?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I did it, yes, sir, once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you did that, how were you able to establish that the casualties or the injured persons that you saw were indeed injured from the incident you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Frankly, when it was the time difference between the incident and the UNMO reaching there, myself, in one case, I [indiscernible] a place. I think it was Butmir probably, and there were certain flesh of the body, even found in that area. And when asked, they said they have moved one of the dead body to one of the morgues close by. So I went there. They were injured. You cannot just say that probably the injury has been caused just a few minutes back, so that is the only reason; otherwise, I can't say that -- it is merely the -- time of injury and you reaching there is between 15 or 20 minutes. So you can make out whether it is this injury or not. If you're asking me whether it was -- the reason was something else, I would say maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you were talking -- you were about to explain the incident on the 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: You want me to give the entire --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me ask you one question before you do give an explanation. Do you recall what that incident was caused by, what kind of weapon caused that incident?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The one that --

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Should I give the entire answer now? Right. It was 1st of July when the incident -- I have my birthday -- my wife birthday is 1st of July, and now I also after this incident celebrate my birthday. I thought probably I got another life. I was sitting and writing a letter to my wife, and it was in one room. It was a two-storey house. The lower portion was with the landlord, his wife and his son and his daughter-in-law. We were on the second, we had the office there, the kitchen and it was on the first floor, and second was mainly the accommodation. So I was sitting in the kitchen on a table writing a letter, and the rest of the team, they were sitting in the so-called office, and they was enjoying -- probably it was one of the team members' national day, Canadian or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm very sorry, I loathe to interrupt you. I just want to ask one or two questions from what you said just now. You said it was a two-storey his house with your landlord, his wife, his son. Were these people civilians or military?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And secondly, do you recall what time of day or night it was?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I think it was around -- should be 9.00, 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: 2100 hours. So I was writing the letter. The other fellow that was sitting in the room, and then we -- one of my colleagues shouted, and that was a normal practice there. I mean, when there used to be a fire-arm, the things I'm talking of is only our first one or two months, that is June, July. Later on things were different. So that was a difficult time. So we used to listen to this noise I think coming from one side or the other side, so you could hear the noise, a whistle-like noise. So one of my -- and they used to shout, There is something coming. So somebody shouted from the other room that there is something big coming. They heard a noise, and we all thought probably it will go off and fall somewhere else. So in about, I think, a few seconds' time, when there was no noise, and after about ten seconds there was a big explosion, and I could only -- I mean, I was sitting like the way now I am sitting, and on the right was the window. So the entire window that unhinged from that wall had just fallen on me, on my face was on the right. I just fell down. I had some injuries there on the right shoulder and then I was on my left leg. That was comparatively a little more serious. And this happened because of the glass of the window and the wood of the window. And the leg was basically, I think there was some glass piece which went inside and it caused a little more damage. So that was it. And thereafter there was no light, and there was a huge bang, and after about five -- I mean, a few seconds, we thought that probably -- I mean, there was no casualties, serious casualties. Everybody started shouting. I was breathing on -- one of the other colleague, a Bangladeshi officer, he was from air force, he also was injured, and the rest of us, we were closer to the roadside, so the other people on the left side, they were safe. So there was no light, so we could only -- I mean, they helped us to go up to the bathroom, which was close by, so that they can clean our faces and remove the blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me ask you: You said that somebody shouted from the other room that there was something big coming. What was it that -- what was it that made him describe this as something big coming; do you know?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Who described it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was the noise -- I mean, when you are sitting underneath, or when it is something big, so you can hear the noise before that. It's something like a rocket or maybe fighter aircraft. I mean, it is something like that. That is the -- something. And why people used to shout, because it was a normal practice in those days, just to alert everybody. It was normal practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say it was normal practice, do you mean that this -- this occurrence was regular or frequent while you were in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I say, yes, for first few days. I'm talking of the first few days it was. But later on, the things were different. There was nothing -- thereafter, I was -- should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I just want to make one clarification. I understood when you started your answer that you said for the first few months.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And now you're saying for the first few days.

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: The first few months, yes, one or two months. Till 1st July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to get that clear because -- So you -- were you able to -- or was it established what kind of projectile caused this -- caused your injuries and caused this incident?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Frankly, because I was injured, I was evacuated initially to the Hrasnica hospital and then to one of the French hospital [sic], and I had some stitches, and thereafter I was kept there in Sarajevo, as in Sarajevo -- one of the other team. So I will not say that I had seen all this, but later on I was told that probably it was one of the modified bomb with some additional explosive and additional rockets which may gave it a little more range and a little more force. So that was ... probably was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this modified bomb with additional rockets, you said that the rockets gave it more range and more force. Can you say anything about its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I was told -- I mean, no. Regarding accuracy, there are two things: One is with the direct firing weapons; and the second is the one that now we are talking of. It was -- I mean, something like anti-tank weapons, rockets, or maybe ammunition, so that was so old that it never used to follow the same direction and in most of the cases that was not even exploded. In this case, again, the accuracy was not -- I mean, you have something modified. The simple answer is that the accuracy will be, I mean, unquestionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, upon -- well, was this incident -- was this incident, to your knowledge, investigated?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yes, it was investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were you in any way involved in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: I just gave my statement there in Sarajevo to one of the police officer [sic], I think, and there were a few people who came, and I gave the statement, what happened with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recall whether a report was completed upon the investigation?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could ask for 65 ter 02770 to be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Colonel, in a moment, you will see a document on your screen and I will ask you a couple of questions. Do you see the document there on the right-hand side, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And from the subject, does it appear to you to be an official authentic UN document on the incident that you just spoken about?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: It is a report of the Hrasnica bombing incident on the 1st of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You see your name on that page, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I believe the -- Captain Frank Melum. This is the --

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: The team leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. Now three of them have signatures, and you have not -- there's no signature for you. Can you tell the Court why is that?

utterances.speaker: IJAZ HUSSAIN MALIK
utterances.text: Maybe I think I was evacuated to some other place. It was Hrasnica and I was evacuated to Sarajevo. My second month as a -- [indiscernible] both were injured. I mean, we were serious -- not very serious. I mean, we were comparatively more seriously injured, so we were transported in a French APC to the French hospital in Sarajevo, so maybe that is the reason why it is not signed. But I think I have signed one or a document of this, maybe one. I had definitely signed that statement that I had been given. But this could be the reason, that I wasn't there; I was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this document be tendered into evidence -- or be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P635, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder whether -- I understand we're stopping at 5.00. I wonder whether ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn until next Tuesday at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.59 p.m.,
